brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.
requirements.evidence: Built: half-e base at (0,0,0) carrying a slide-style west-half drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut), plus a spike at junction (0,0)|(0,1)|(1,0) (spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0). Both are fitted to cell (0,0,0), and check_build reports meshClash 'clear'. However, I could not confirm from the tools that the drawer's cut face and the spike's corner coincide exactly; the spike sits at the three-cell junction and the drawer sits on the cut face of the same cell, so 'same corner' is likely but not verified. The 'touching' condition was not measured directly beyond the mesh check passing.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
